decision: scoped ten features plus e2e into 7 batches ordered by dependency (roles and audit first, offline and e2e last)
why: audit needs a user identity, banner and sold-out are small, offline and LINE are the risky ones

decision: roles and audit log landed together: Admin extractor on setup/takings routes, audit rows on confirm/cancel/skip/reset/staff
why: audit needs a who, so identity came first; Authed stayed for tills so existing handlers did not change

decision: close-day report, password on reset, backup download plus daily copy in one batch
why: all three protect the shop from its own mistakes and share the audit hooks and Admin gate from batch 1

decision: kept the backup on the same disk by default and said so in the UI instead of adding cloud upload
why: an upload target needs the user's account and keys, and a download button already gives a copy off the machine
result: open: user may want S3 later

decision: till warning bar and sold-out switch
why: both are small and touch the same pos.js; health answer is cached 20s so many tills do not hammer the verify API
evidence: commit e49af93, 107 backend tests, browser check of banner and sold-out tile

decision: notes on lines and orders, discount on the bill, reason when cancelling
why: the server works out the discount so a stale page cannot change the price, and paying back a paid order must leave a written reason
evidence: backend tests 113 pass, frontend tests 37 pass, clicked through POS in the browser (discount, notes, cancel reason, dashboard)

decision: LINE message when a queue is called: customer signs in with LIFF, server verifies the ID token with LINE, shop's own OA pushes
why: an ID token checked by LINE is the only thing that proves whose account it is; the push never blocks calling the queue
evidence: backend 115 tests incl. pretend LINE (verify + push), browser check of the queue-page button and the settings card; real LINE sign-in NOT run (needs a real LINE channel)

decision: cash sales with no connection are kept in the till's browser and sent later, oldest first
why: the till makes an id per sale so a retry or a reload can never double-sell; a sale the server refuses is kept with its reason instead of being lost
evidence: backend 118 tests (retry, race, bad id, sold out), frontend 47 tests incl. 10 for the offline queue, browser check: cut fetch, sold 2 cash orders, restored, one order A003 made and a manual retry returned the same order

decision: end-to-end test: real binary, pretend payment API, pretend LINE; sell, pay, call, LINE push; added to CI
why: unit tests cannot show that the poller, the one-QR lock, the slip and the LINE push work together; a run against the built program can
evidence: frontend/tests/e2e/flow.e2e.js 2 tests pass; breaking the LINE push on purpose made it fail with a timeout, then restored
